title: Small transit pings work but OSPF will not reach FULL
scenario: On an isolated Ethernet lab, R1 and R2 previously reached FULL. R1 was changed to ip mtu 1400 without a design requirement. Both NICs and the direct link support the approved 1500-byte IPv4 MTU. The router IDs are unique, area/timers match, and no mtu-ignore override is configured. Small transit pings still succeed.

exhibits.title: Representative neighbor and IP interface state
exhibits.text:
R1 neighbor 2.2.2.2: EXSTART
R1 Gi0/0/1 IP MTU: 1400
R2 Gi0/0/0 IP MTU: 1500

exhibits.title: Authored packet observation
exhibits.text:
R2 database-description packet advertises interface MTU 1500.
R1 rejects that DBD under its 1400-byte interface-MTU check.
Approved direct-link IP MTU: 1500 on both routers.

question: Which correction addresses the demonstrated failure while retaining MTU validation?
options: Reduce the OSPF hello interval only on R1
Enable ip ospf mtu-ignore at both ends
Restore R1 to the approved 1500-byte IP MTU
Give R1 the same router ID as R2
explanation: The mismatched MTU and rejection observation establish this particular database-exchange failure. A small ping does not test the same condition, and EXSTART by itself would not identify a unique cause.
fix:
Restore the documented value in this isolated lab:

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R1(config-if)# ip mtu 1500
R1(config-if)# end
R1# show ip interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
R1# show ip route
```

Verify the peer, required routes and application return path after convergence. On an actual constrained path, determine a mutually supported MTU from evidence rather than raising it blindly or bypassing the check. After confirming both route directions, repeat the permitted USERS/PC-A HTTP request to SRV and retain the intended STAFF/PC-B HTTP denial. Record fresh requests rather than relying on an old page.

title: Clients cannot renew after a switch security change
scenario: After DHCP snooping is enabled for VLAN 20, client renewal fails while static clients still communicate. The approved DHCP server is reachable only through SW2 Gi0/1. The collected evidence explicitly identifies a legitimate server OFFER arriving there and being discarded; endpoint ports should remain untrusted.

exhibits.title: Representative configuration
exhibits.text:
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 20
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 switchport mode trunk
 ! no ip dhcp snooping trust configured

exhibits.title: Authored observation record
exhibits.text:
Snooping operational VLANs: 20
Client DISCOVER: leaves Gi0/1 toward approved server
Legitimate DHCPOFFER: received on Gi0/1
Drop reason: DHCP server message on untrusted ingress port

question: Which correction matches the evidence without trusting clients?
options: Disable snooping globally on every switch
Trust the verified server-facing Gi0/1 ingress
Trust every VLAN 20 client access port
Change the working client gateway to the server
explanation: The observed OFFER is rejected on the verified server-facing ingress because it remains untrusted. The server has already responded, so an unproven claim that option 82 prevented every response does not explain this observation.
fix:
After confirming Gi0/1’s physical and logical path to the approved server, configure that interface:

```ios
SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW2(config-if)# ip dhcp snooping trust
SW2(config-if)# end
SW2# show ip dhcp snooping
SW2# show ip dhcp snooping binding
```

Renew the client and verify the OFFER/ACK path, correct lease and learned binding. Keep endpoint ports untrusted. Do not add an arbitrary low DHCP rate limit during recovery; size such limits for the actual client traffic and platform. Confirm gateway reachability and the original application test from the renewed client. The binding and the end-to-end result answer different questions.
